scenes.visual: Big navy hook text pops in word by word; Norb peeks from below, curious.
scenes.cardText: It's not the stress. It's your rank.
scenes.voiceover: Stress isn't what's wearing you down. Where you sit in the pecking order is.

scenes.visual: Rank ladder: three creatures on ascending pillars; the bottom-rank one trembles and sweats, the top wears a crown. Norb watches, alarmed.
scenes.voiceover: Take a troop of baboons. Same savanna, same threats. The ones at the bottom get sick the most.

scenes.visual: Cortisol drop character looks frazzled while dots loop endlessly; Norb is exhausted.
scenes.voiceover: Low rank means low control. So the stress alarm never shuts off, and that slow drip wears the body down.

scenes.visual: A surge wave swells and finally passes beside a steady anchor; Norb gets the idea.
scenes.voiceover: You can't always climb the ladder. But control and connection turn that alarm back down.

scenes.visual: THE SCIENCE card; below it a bar chart where cortisol rises as social rank falls (low-rank bar tallest); Norb curious.
scenes.cardText:
It's not the stressor.
Low rank and low control keep cortisol high — that's the damage.
scenes.voiceover: Here's the science. From baboons to office workers, it's not the workload. Low rank and low control keep cortisol high. That's the real damage.

scenes.visual: TRY THIS card; below it two creatures slide together and a warm pulse calms the stressed one; Norb celebrates.
scenes.cardText:
You can't pick your rank.
So take back one thing you control.
Text one person you trust.
scenes.voiceover: You can't change your rank overnight. But you can take back one thing you control today. Then text one person you trust — that connection is the off switch.
